papers.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
papers.abstract: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$\beta$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

papers.title: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
papers.abstract: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

papers.title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
papers.abstract: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfv\'en waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware bandwidth selection for smoothed charge deposition in 2D electrostatic particle-in-cell
papers.abstract: Charge deposition in the particle-in-cell (PIC) method can be viewed as kernel density estimation on a spatial mesh. This allows the smoothing bandwidth to be selected through statistical criteria such as mean integrated squared error or cross-validation, but it also changes the electric field acting on the particles. Therefore, a selected bandwidth can alter the growth or damping of physical modes. We develop a dynamics-aware bandwidth-selection procedure that combines a density-error objective with constraints on specified linear modes. These constraints follow from the plasma equilibrium and the combined transfer of deposition, filtering and field gathering within the model rate-tolerance boundary. We demonstrate the need for equilibrium information through a controlled two-stream experiment. The controlled two-stream scan varies the beam drift while holding the initial spatial density, thermal samples, wavevector and fixed-filter transfer unchanged. Across four resolved equilibria approaching marginal stability, this filter reduces the measured growth rate by $0.7\%$ to $9.1\%$. Equilibrium-dependent interior settings satisfy the prescribed $10\%$ rate tolerance. We then apply the constrained selection rule to 85 Gaussian candidates, that reduces density and grid-field mean-square errors by $7.40\%$ and $3.70\%$ on independently evaluated snapshots. A separate projected-linear calculation at that exact width gives a ratio of mean individual growth rates of $0.9556$, with paired $95\%$ interval $[0.9453,0.9640]$, consistent with the prediction $0.9513$. Analysis of finite-marker loading and ensemble averaging explains how the measured rates relate to the response model. Together, these results demonstrate a filter-design procedure that combines statistical error reduction with subsequent validation of the selected linear dynamics.

papers.title: A generative foundation model for 2D magnetized plasma turbulence
papers.abstract: We present a proof-of-principle study demonstrating a conditional generative foundation model for self-organizing magnetized plasma turbulence. Built on a multichannel flow-matching framework with a spectral decomposition strategy, the model is trained on direct numerical simulations of 2D modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (MHW) turbulence across the hydrodynamic to adiabatic parameter range. Without retraining, this \textit{single} model successfully performs three distinct downstream tasks: (i) unconditional generation of statistically faithful quasi-steady-state snapshots that recover the directional energy spectra and amplitude statistics, from which statistical transport quantities, including turbulent flux and effective diffusivity, alongside their uncertainties, are inferred directly; (ii) super-resolution from $4\times$ and $8\times$ downsampled observations to reconstruct fine-scale turbulence and large-scale zonal structures; and (iii) full-field inpainting from sparse spatial observations covering as little as $\sim 10\%$ of the domain. The generated fields faithfully reproduce regime-dependent turbulence vs. zonal-flow states and energy partitioning. Under extreme sparsity the long-correlation zonal flows are pinned by only a handful of observations, while the residual uncertainty concentrates in the small-scale turbulent fluctuations. These results establish flow-matching generative models as powerful, unified surrogates for state generation, statistical inference, and sparse-data reconstruction, providing a scalable baseline for 3D plasma turbulence and experimental applications.

papers.title: Neutron-Lean D-3He Fusion by Asymmetric Enhancement of the Primary Reaction: A Spin-Polarized Non-Thermal Hot Tail
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on a modified fuel that combines the theory of spin-polarized fuel with non-thermal "hot-tail" reactions for D-T, D-3He, and D-D reactions. We find that this combination is particularly advantageous for the D-3He fuel in several respects. First, a large reactivity enhancement: one order of magnitude at 10 keV for a small hot tail (F = 0.1), rising to two orders of magnitude for a larger one (F = 0.6), with polarization adding a further factor of 1.5. Second, an ideal ignition energy far below the thermal value: 9.5 keV at F = 0.3 down to 3.2 keV at F = 0.5, which polarization reduces further to 3.8 keV and 1.3 keV, respectively. Third, the asymmetric enhancement between the primary reaction and the secondary reactions in the fuel opens the possibility of a neutron-lean reaction. Quantifying this with a neutrons-per-watt metric, we find that a thermal D-3He plasma at 10 keV is barely neutron-lean at all (90-95% of the D-T neutron rate per watt), whereas a hot tail of F = 0.1 reduces it by 4.7-7.7x and the polarized non-thermal fuel at its ignition point reaches 3.0-5.4% of the D-T value, with only 0.4-2.4% of the fusion power carried by neutrons. The range spans prompt removal versus complete in-situ burnup of the bred tritium. Applied to a 200 MW worked example anchored on the ARTEMIS D-3He reactor design, this is a first-wall neutron loading of 0.008-0.043 MW/m^2 against 1.45 MW/m^2 for D-T in the same chamber, extending the time to reach 20 dpa from about 1.5 full-power years to 27.

papers.title: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the EAST tokamak
papers.abstract: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) is reported in this work. In this regime, internal transport barriers(ITBs) and a flat core safety factor profile were maintained simultaneously by fishbone modes. First,the drive of low-frequency flows by fishbone modes is clarified, which subsequently suppresses turbulence transport. Besides, fishbone-induced poloidally symmetric (m = 0) toroidal current sheets were first reported experimentally, which drive outward current redistribution that mitigates core current peaking. Together, these effects enable hybrid operation with stable ITBs and robust magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability, revealing a self-organized pathway for sustaining hybrid scenario for fusion reactors.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of tungsten armor and a liquid-lithium film as first walls for the HiPER laser-fusion chamber: thermal response, vapor shielding and helium transmission to the steel
papers.abstract: Tungsten armor and liquid-metal films, the usual sacrificial first walls of laser-fusion chambers, were modeled separately. Both go through one calculation for the three HiPER scenarios: NRL 154 MJ spectra scaled by yield, binned to keep each ion species' number and energy, a common deposition model, and a one-dimensional enthalpy solver with melting, evaporation and parameterized vapor shielding. In Demo (154 MJ, 6.5 m, 10 Hz), a 1 mm tungsten armor peaks 378 K below melting without neutron heating (275-319 K with it). A degraded near-surface conductivity can erase this margin, which also depends on the ion-spectra construction. The steel interface exceeds the 925 K limit, and the surface accumulates the 10^18-10^19 m^-2 helium fluences associated with the onset of surface modification within 10-98 shots (not a lifetime). A lithium film keeps the steel below 925 K from 44 um and below the 873 K compatibility limit from 56 um, more with partial renewal. Burn ions then implant helium; keeping the steel below 10^18 m^-2 for 10^6 shots needs 184 um, which binds in every scenario. The film evaporates 7.4x10^-4 kg m^-2 per shot (range 4.2-8.4x10^-4 kg m^-2, full renewal). Vapor shielding, with a nearly un-ionized vapor (Saha estimate), changes this by -21 % to +5 % for the Saha-supported stopping factor s = 1 and -34 % to +8 % across s = 1-2. Both walls are thermally viable in Prototype and marginal for tungsten in Demo. The deciding issues are tungsten damage evolution, lithium film survival and chamber clearing.

papers.title: A Comparison of Electric-Field Profile Reconstruction Methods based on the E-FISH Diagnostic
papers.abstract: Electric-field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH) is a non-intrusive, non-resonant technique for measuring electric fields in moderate-to-atmospheric pressure plasmas. However, its nonlinear, path-integrated nature introduces measurement uncertainty, preventing a unique relationship between the measured signal and local electric field. One approach to overcome this limitation is to acquire spatial EFISH profiles and invert them to reconstruct the underlying electric-field distribution. Although several inversion methods have been employed, their reconstruction accuracy and overall performance have yet to be systematically evaluated. This study compares three methods: machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion, using EFISH measurements from four electrode geometries with distinct electric-field distributions. Their performance is evaluated in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness to sparse data and noise, and ability to reconstruct asymmetric profiles. All three methods successfully reconstruct electric-field profiles, but exhibit distinct advantages and limitations. Machine learning provides high accuracy, computational speed, and noise resilience, but performs poorly on profiles that differ substantially from its training data, particularly asymmetric profiles. Linear inversion accommodates a broader range of field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile. Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields but performs well for horizontal field polarization. The complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivate a potential hybrid approach for reconstructing electric fields with unknown spatial distributions. Overall, this study identifies key trade-offs among the methods and provides guidance for selecting suitable reconstruction strategies under different measurement conditions.

papers.title: Recovering Non-Maxwellian Velocity Distribution Functions from Collective Thomson Scattering Spectra Using Generalized Basis Representations
papers.abstract: Thomson scattering (TS) is a key diagnostic for inferring plasma parameters from scattered power spectra, but its interpretation depends strongly on assumptions about the underlying velocity distribution functions (VDFs). Conventional analyses typically assume Maxwellian distributions, which can be invalid in high-energy-density and laboratory astrophysics plasmas where collisionless, multi-population dynamics produce non-thermal features. In such cases, Maxwellian models may reproduce observed spectra while yielding inaccurate or misleading plasma parameters. We present a generalized TS analysis framework that represents species-specific VDFs in flexible, physically motivated bases and so reconstructs complex, non-equilibrium distributions. To explore the resulting high-dimensional parameter space, we build the forward model from differentiable operations and optimize the VDF parameters by gradient descent. We apply the method to synthetic TS spectra generated from particle-in-cell simulations of a collisionless shock with interacting hydrogen and carbon populations. Immediately upstream of the shock, where the plasma is most non-thermal, the flexible bases cut the mean normalized ion VDF residual from 38.7% for a Maxwellian model to 20.3% and 20.5%, with correspondingly improved time-resolved plasma parameters. We also introduce a systematic method of uncertainty quantification that reveals degeneracies between ion species, highlighting the importance of both flexible VDF modeling and a statistical mapping of the solution space for this inherently ill-posed inversion problem.

papers.title: Relativistic Chiral MHD with application to the early Universe
papers.abstract: We present a systematic derivation of the equations of relativistic chiral magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) for a plasma of charged fermions in an expanding universe. Through a combination of a coordinate transformation and a rescaling of the dynamical variables, we bring the full system to the same form as in the Minkowski metric, with the Hubble expansion surviving only in the chirality-flipping rate and the kinematic viscosity. Retaining all four contributions to both the electric and the axial current yields terms absent from standard chiral MHD: charge-density corrections to the evolution equations for the chemical potentials, and an electric current proportional to the charge chemical potential $\mu$ and the bulk velocity. The latter is mandated by current conservation, requires no chirality imbalance, and drives the charge-flow instability studied in a follow-up paper. For the radiation-dominated era, we evaluate all the coefficients in physical units and use them to estimate the magnetic Reynolds number, the attainable magnetic field strength, and the minimum temperature at which the chiral dynamo can operate. The resulting equations are cast in a form ready for direct numerical implementation.

papers.title: Nonthermal Particle Acceleration by Magnetic Pumping in Pulsating Plasmas
papers.abstract: We present a new pulsating box setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression--expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results could be relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in certain high-beta space and astrophysical plasmas.

papers.title: Non-Ambipolarity of Microturbulent Transport
papers.abstract: When exact magnetic surfaces are assumed to exist, the gyrokinetic theory of microturbulence gives the same radial transport for ions and electrons. But, exact magnetic surfaces do not exist in the presence of what is called electrostatic microturbulence. When the plasma pressure is non-zero, a turbulent electric potential is accompanied by a turbulent magnetic field, which splits the rational magnetic surfaces with which it resonates. If the magnetic field is assumed to have an ideal topology-conserving evolution, delta function current densities arise on resonant surfaces. The singularity of the current density allows islands to open quickly, but there is no singularity that allows a rapid closure. Islands remain and do not flutter into and out of existence. A relative rotation of the electron fluid in neighboring island chains produces a non-dissipative force that can lock the islands together and produce a non-ambipolar transport. At sufficient plasma pressure, the islands associated with different resonant rational surfaces can overlap. When this occurs some magnetic field lines will cross the entire radial region occupied by overlapping islands. The effect on the electron fluid is to create a viscosity-like force, which is dissipative and tends to remove gradients in the electron rotation. This also produces a non-ambipolar transport. Under many assumptions, the island locking force is larger than the viscosity-like force.

papers.title: Pfirsch-Schl\"uter Current
papers.abstract: The Pfirsch-Schl\"uter current is a current that flows along the magnetic field lines in a toroidal plasma equilibrium that is required to make the plasma current density divergence free in the presence of a plasma-pressure gradient. A distortion in the plasma shape is caused by the Pfirsch-Schl\"uter current, and it is desirable to minimize both the strength and the distance this current flows along the magnetic field lines. The Pfirsch-Schl\"uter current is localized within a half period of a stellarator when $d\ell/B$ integrated over the half period is the same for all lines in the magnetic surface. It is shown that within parts in a thousand this is the same condition as the distance $\ell_{s}$ required for a field line to cross the half period being the same for all lines in the surface. To make the $\ell_{s}$'s the same, the lines started on the small major radius side of the plasma must undergo wiggles to make their $\ell_{s}$ as long as those started on the outboard side. This is generally achieved using modular coils with a large helical component on the small major radius side but could be achieved with a central column carrying a helical current.

papers.title: Rapid Vacuum Response Calculations for Non-axisymmetric Plasma Geometries
papers.abstract: We present a fast, open-source calculation of the vacuum response matrix and surface inductance in non-axisymmetric geometries capable of running with up to 10^5 boundary points in tens of seconds on a laptop. Ideal magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) stability modeling for free boundary modes requires the perturbed vacuum energy. We extend the VACUUM code to non-axisymmetric geometries in the new Julia implementation of the Generalized Perturbed Equilibrium Code, combining a collocation approach to the boundary integral equations with a high-order singularity correction scheme. The correction is recast into explicit quadrature weights acting on the collocation values, which allows the corrected operator to be assembled explicitly rather than applied to a given surface field, and the structure of that matrix under field-period and stellarator symmetry is then exploited to reduce storage and solve cost. We find that the vacuum response matrix converges at fourth order or greater in the grid spacing, reaching a given accuracy on a coarser grid than previous implementations without the high-order method. The non-axisymmetric calculation converges to the axisymmetric VACUUM result for a tokamak and the CAS3D result for a W7-X stellarator equilibrium. This work enables fast free boundary ideal MHD stability and perturbed equilibrium calculations in stellarators.

papers.title: Experimental verification of the PRIORA Monte Carlo code for proton radiography
papers.abstract: PRIORA (Proton Radiography Ion-Optical Ray-tracing Analysis) is a fast Monte Carlo model for high-energy proton radiography. It combines fitted proton-matter interaction tables with energy-dependent transfer maps of arbitrary order and simulates approximately $10^6$ protons/s through a complete ion-optical system on an 8-core laptop. We verify it with GSI data obtained with the Ta_bench target: fifteen precision slits in a 2 mm Ta plate between symmetric PMMA staircases. A single experimental image provides the image scale, spatial resolution as a function of chromatic load, the direction of longitudinal defocus in both transverse planes, effective angular acceptance and multiple-scattering contrast. With identical processing of experiment and simulation and no physics adjustment, PRIORA reproduces the data obtained with 2 and 4 GeV protons. At 2 GeV, PRIORA also recovers sub-percent quadrupole trims consistent with the control-system records and determines a target-plane spatial resolution of $115\pm6\,\mu$m.
